target: Commercialization addition: free Arcanum tools vs the intent-bug human-review problem
convergence: Free tools do NOT reduce human intent review (it is irreducible, and LLM-authored specs can ratify a shared intent error). They RELOCATE it upstream (code-diff -> spec/definition, amortizable) and REFOCUS it into structured, mechanically-gated, auditable fidelity reports + first-class residue. The honest claim is 'intent review made cheaper, unskippable, and legible', not 'reduced' -- and that reframe is STRONGER commercially because legible+immutable intent-review trail IS the SOC2/ITGC paid-attestation value.
load_bearing_residue: Design constraint (mandatory, not caveat): humans must own the spec/definition ground truth and the gates must ADD friction at intent-critical points, or circularity + automation-bias make escaped intent bugs WORSE. Measurement gap: no study shows these specific tools reduce escaped intent bugs (LLM oracle accuracy ~48-54%).
recommended_next_routes: decision-gate (commit the 'relocate+legibilize, not reduce' framing + the human-owns-spec design constraint as a product requirement)
task-session (instrument escaped-intent-bug + review-time measurement on the spec->test pipeline to close the measurement gap)
refine (design the friction-at-intent-critical-points UX so tools counter automation bias rather than feed it)
